category: relay/P2P — SIGNALLING with encrypted fallback transport

free_tier.stated: iroh includes a set of public relays provided by n0.computer, available to all iroh users at no cost.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: Public relays forward end-to-end encrypted packets and state no single-object size limit; the relays are signalling with an encrypted transport fallback, not object storage. Absence is not an unlimited claim.

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: Relays are stateless and the free Community tier states 7 day metrics retention; the public-relay page states no retention period for forwarded bytes. Absence is not an unlimited claim.

egress.terms: Free public relays, rate-limited. Self-hosting a relay is free and unlimited (open licence). The cost moves to your own bandwidth.

interface_detail: QUIC over TLS 1.3; Rust crate `iroh`, bindings for other languages
tooling: `iroh` crate; relay is a library, not a service with an upload endpoint
chaining: This is SIGNALLING, not relaying, in the normal case: 'roughly 9 out of 10 connections go direct; the relay is only a fallback'. The relay carries bytes only when hole punching fails, which is what makes the free tier viable at all.
limits_note: Not a storage provider. Only relayed bytes hit the operator, hence the per-connection rate limit rather than a byte quota.
reliability_note: 'The exact rate limits aren't published today, as they get tuned as needed' and 'Do not rely on it for production workloads'. The free tier is explicitly capacity-unstable by design.
confidence_note: the public relays are stated as free to all iroh users on the Public Relays page

extras.agent_focus: Systematic sweep of self-hosted academic repository software (Dataverse, DSpace, InvenioRDM, EPrints, Fedora/Islandora) scored on the four client questions: institutional-email requirement, per-file cap, per-collection/dataset cap, and whether the install enforces a quota object at all. Primary method was machine probing, not page reading: /api/info/version and /api/dataverses/:root/storage/quota?showInherited=true against the full official Dataverse installation registry (150 hostnames), the native-signup form probe /dataverseuser.xhtml?editMode=CREATE against all 83 no-quota hosts, and the platform source defaults read out of the upstream config files for DSpace, InvenioRDM, EPrints, libp2p and iroh. Secondary coverage of the relay/P2P half of the slot.
